newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - New drugs to drive SmithKline in Q3.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - New drugs to drive SmithKline in Q3.

text.p: Anglo-American drugs group SmithKline Beecham Plc is expected to announce another strong set of quarterly results on Tuesday with new products again driving profits forward, analysts said on Friday.

Forecasts for pre-tax profit are in an unusually tight range of between 370.0 and 375.0 million stg compared with 310 million a year earlier, with the dividend of 4.0 pence in line with the first two quarters.
Strong drugs growth is expected to be the major feature once more, led by the anti-depressent and panic disorder treatment Paxil/Seroxat.
Paxil, which competes head-on with Eli Lilly & Co's Prozac, has been taking market share in a fast-expanding field.
"This drug could be a $2 billion drug by the year 2000," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
A twice-daily formulation of Augmentin is also expected to have further boosted the fast-growing antibiotic's market share.

Alyson Coates, analyst at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull, said she expected pharmaceuticals sales growth of 15 percent in the third quarter, including the pharmaceutical benefit manager DPS. She saw Paxil and the group's important vaccine business driving the growth.
Analysts said they would be attempting to penetrate the mysteries surrounding pharmacy benefit manager DPS, which SmithKline has kept quiet about since acquiring it in 1994.
Suggestions that rival Eli Lilly is considering writing down the value of its pharmacy benefit management unit have caused some nervousness.

Analysts will be looking for signs of increased recruitment at DPS. There was some disappointment that the total number of lives covered at the end of the second quarter was virtually unchanged from the first quarter at around 30 million.
Analysts at Lehman Brothers warned in the summer: "We will need to see a considerable improvement in either covered lives or profit per life" if DPS was to do more than break even."

SGST's Coates said she would be looking for signs of improved cash generation, with SmithKline's debt levels remaining stubborbly high, and for a pick-up in profit margins at the over-the-counter business, where the group had invested heavily in promotion and advertising.
One black cloud which continues to hang over the group is the resolution of a dispute with the U.S. government over alleged overcharging by its Clinical Laboratories operations.
SmithKline took a provision of 250 million stg last year to cover any damages arising from the issue, and press reports last month suggested the two sides might be close to a $300 million settlment.
